title: Design Trade-Offs between Target Binding and Self-Association Revealed by De Novo SARS-CoV-2 Binders.
authors: Carcelen, Lourdes; Penas-Utrilla, Daniel; Ferrero, Diego S; Ferrer-Orta, Cristina; Nadal, Marta; Colizzi, Francesco; Munoz, Juana C; Taules, Marta; Verdaguer, Nuria; Marcos, Enrique
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过整合AlphaFold预测、MD模拟、对接和SAP计算，系统解析了从头设计SARS-CoV-2结合蛋白中靶标结合与自聚集之间的权衡机制，并据此理性重设计出稳定单体且具微摩尔亲和力的变体，直接贡献于蛋白质结构计算设计方法。
abstract: De novo protein binders have emerged as a powerful platform for molecular recognition, yet achieving high affinity while maintaining favorable biophysical properties remains a major challenge. Here, using the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) as a model target, we generated two de novo protein binder design campaigns that deliberately imposed different trade-offs between binding and monomeric behavior, and benchmarked them against a set of experimentally validated binders. Through integrated experimental and computational analyses, we show that binder design is constrained by two distinct failure modes that require different optimization strategies. None of the 22 original designs showed measurable binding to the RBD, with one class remaining monomeric but failing to achieve sufficient target binding, while the other had more competent binding interfaces but exhibited excessive surface hydrophobicity that promoted self-association. By integrating AlphaFold-based predictions, molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and surface aggregation propensity (SAP) calculations, we establish complementary computational signatures that distinguish these failure modes and reveal their underlying structural determinants. Guided by these insights, we prospectively redesigned a representative failed binder by reducing noninterface hydrophobicity while preserving folding and binding interface quality. Experimental characterization by SEC-MALS, surface plasmon resonance, and circular dichroism confirmed that the redesigned variants were stable monomers and acquired low muM binding affinities. Together, our results define the mechanistic trade-offs between binding and self-association in de novo protein binder design and provide a framework for diagnosing and rationally overcoming common design failure modes.
abstract_zh: 从头设计蛋白结合物已成为分子识别的一个强大平台，然而在保持良好生物物理性质的同时实现高亲和力仍是一项重大挑战。在此，以SARS-CoV-2受体结合域（RBD）为模型靶标，我们开展了两个从头设计蛋白结合物的设计活动，这些活动有意施加了结合与单体行为之间的不同权衡，并针对一组经实验验证的结合物进行了基准测试。通过整合实验和计算分析，我们表明结合物设计受到两种不同失败模式的制约，这些模式需要不同的优化策略。22个原始设计中无一显示出对RBD的可测量结合，其中一类保持单体状态但未能达到足够的靶标结合，而另一类具有更有效的结合界面，但表现出过度的表面疏水性，促进了自缔合。通过整合基于AlphaFold的预测、分子动力学模拟、对接分析和表面聚集倾向性（SAP）计算，我们建立了区分这些失败模式的互补计算特征，并揭示了其潜在的结构决定因素。在这些见解的指导下，我们前瞻性地重新设计了一个代表性的失败结合物，通过减少非界面疏水性同时保留折叠和结合界面质量。通过SEC-MALS、表面等离子体共振和圆二色性的实验表征确认，重新设计的变体是稳定的单体，并获得了低微摩尔级的结合亲和力。总体而言，我们的结果定义了对从头设计蛋白结合物中结合与自缔合之间的机制权衡，并为诊断和理性克服常见设计失败模式提供了一个框架。
